title: Add graceful shutdown with health‑check endpoint
description: Implements a production‑grade graceful shutdown that stops accepting new requests on SIGTERM while allowing in‑flight requests to finish, and adds a /health endpoint that reflects server readiness. This reduces downtime during deployments and improves observability for load balancers and orchestrators.
testCases: Verify that GET /health returns 200 and JSON {status:"ok"} while the server is running
Send a SIGTERM to the process, ensure new connections receive 503 and existing connections complete before the process exits
acceptance: When the process receives SIGTERM, the server stops listening for new connections, responds with 503 to any new request, waits for all active requests to finish (with a configurable timeout), then exits. The /health endpoint returns 200 when the server is ready and 503 after shutdown has begun. All tests pass and no regression in existing routing or middleware.
reason: Enables zero‑downtime deployments and reliable health monitoring in containerized environments, addressing a critical production need for stability and observability.
